links.detail: On 14 August 2020 Angola's Supreme Court convicted former governor Valter Filipe (eight years), BNA manager Samalia (five years), José Filomeno dos Santos (five years) and businessman Sebastião (six years) of embezzlement, fraud and influence peddling over an attempted illicit transfer of $500 million to a London account, which a British bank blocked. After the Constitutional Court annulled the ruling, the Supreme Court plenary confirmed the convictions in 2024.
links.src_t: Tribunal Supremo confirma condenações no caso '500 milhões' (Ver Angola / Lusa)

links.detail: In October 2011 RBA subsidiaries Securency and NPA pleaded guilty to conspiring to bribe foreign officials to win banknote business with note-issuing authorities of Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and Nepal; they paid proceeds-of-crime penalties of A$19.8 million and A$1.86 million and fines of A$480,000 and A$450,000. Securency's former CFO received a suspended six-month sentence for false accounting (2012) and agent Radius Christanto a suspended two-year sentence (2013).
links.src_t: Chronology: Events related to charges against Note Printing Australia and Securency (Reserve Bank of Australia)

links.detail: Former managers of OeBS, the OeNB's banknote printing subsidiary, were tried for paying kickbacks to the central banks of Azerbaijan (20% overcharge) and Syria (14%) to win banknote orders, with about €14 million paid. Seven defendants were convicted in October 2014; after a Supreme Court-ordered retrial, the Vienna court in February 2018 gave Wolf and Miller 18-month suspended terms and Meyer 21 months suspended, while former OeNB deputy governor Duchatczek was acquitted.
links.src_t: More lenient sentence in the second instance in OeBS bribery scandal (CoinsWeekly)

links.detail: Attackers used Bangladesh Bank's SWIFT access on the night of 4 February 2016 to steal reserves from its New York Fed account ($101 million per The Daily Star; $81 million extracted per Prothom Alo). The government inquiry committee's final report of 30 May 2016 hinted at involvement of central bank officials and, according to Prothom Alo, named employees for action; the report was never published and no one was punished as of 2019.

links.detail: A November 2009 internal BEAC report found about 20 billion CFA francs were diverted from the bank's Paris office to 139 beneficiaries between 2004 and 2008. On 28 September 2012 a court in Mfoundi, Cameroon, sentenced Kemadjou to life imprisonment and ordered him to pay BEAC 26.4 billion CFA francs. The BEAC's internal report on the Paris office fraud, published in late October 2009, put the loss at about 25 million euros and described internal controls as far below international standards. It said alarming reports were sent to the governor but no firm action followed, and the article blames governor Mamalépot for not acting and criticizes governor Andzembé for letting the scheme continue. Jean-Pierre Oyiba, chief of staff to Gabon's president, resigned on 9 November 2009 after the report said he received about 100,000 euros, which he denies.
links.src_t: BEAC : Les auteurs du détournement du BEP condamnés (Gabonreview)

links.role: Received money, favors or contracts from the bank
links.detail: A November 2009 internal BEAC report found about 20 billion CFA francs were diverted from the bank's Paris office to 139 beneficiaries between 2004 and 2008. On 28 September 2012 a court in Mfoundi, Cameroon, sentenced Kemadjou to life imprisonment and ordered him to pay BEAC 26.4 billion CFA francs. The BEAC's internal report on the Paris office fraud, published in late October 2009, put the loss at about 25 million euros and described internal controls as far below international standards. It said alarming reports were sent to the governor but no firm action followed, and the article blames governor Mamalépot for not acting and criticizes governor Andzembé for letting the scheme continue. Jean-Pierre Oyiba, chief of staff to Gabon's president, resigned on 9 November 2009 after the report said he received about 100,000 euros, which he denies.
links.src_t: BEAC : Les auteurs du détournement du BEP condamnés (Gabonreview)

links.detail: In May 2015 Banguat president Julio Suárez was arrested with other members of the board of the social security institute (IGSS). Prosecutors said they took part in the irregular award of a 116 million quetzal (about $14.5 million) IGSS contract to the drug company Pisa de Guatemala; the charges listed for the detainees as a group were unlawful association, influence peddling, illegal commissions and active bribery. He was later acquitted: the Supreme Court's Criminal Chamber upheld the June 2019 appeal-court acquittal, as reported in October 2021.
links.src_t: Arrestan a directores de banco central y seguridad social de Guatemala por corrupción (Teletica)

links.detail: In January 2003 impeachment proceedings began against President Luis González Macchi, accused among other things, according to Central Banking, of embezzling US$26m from the central bank. Later reports describe US$16m from two bankrupt private banks taken over by the state. In February 2003 the Senate vote fell short (25 of 44, with 30 needed). A court sentenced him to six years in June 2006, and an appeals court later cleared him, saying the evidence was insufficient.

links.detail: In 2007 Nicaragua's Comptroller General concluded that the Central Bank board sold CENI certificates, issued to cover the collapse of banks, for less than market value and then raised interest rates to benefit the main buyer, Bancentro; the fraud is described as $500 million. The Comptroller alleged criminal involvement by six men, including former finance minister Eduardo Montealegre, who denied wrongdoing and called it a political witch hunt. In July 2008 a special prosecutor filed charges against 39 people including Montealegre; that report names no central bank officials among the accused and gives no court ruling, and it says former Central Bank president Francisco Mayorga was already found guilty in the banking scandal.
links.src_t: Montealegre implicated in banking certificate scandal (Tico Times)

links.role: Paid or bribed the bank's officials
links.detail: A 1991 New York grand-jury indictment of BCCI alleged $3 million in bribes in return for depositing part of Peru's 1986-87 reserves in BCCI's Panama branch; the BCR board approved moving $100 million and later doubling it. The indictment did not name BCR officials; the Christian Science Monitor identified Figueroa and Neyra in the matter, and both strenuously denied the charges, with Neyra calling the decision purely technical. All Peruvian deposits were withdrawn by the end of 1987.

links.detail: After the ECCB seized the Stanford-owned Bank of Antigua, the Official Stanford Investors Committee sued it in Dallas in 2013, alleging it fraudulently misappropriated assets belonging to Stanford's victims and creditors. On 17 August 2018 a US federal judge dismissed the claims in full because the ECCB and Antigua are immune under US foreign sovereign immunity law. The court did not rule on whether the allegations were true.
links.src_t: The Official Stanford Investors Committee v. Bank of Antigua et al, Memorandum Opinion and Order (US District Court, N.D. Texas)

In 2014 he pleaded guilty to six tax offences and was given five months in prison. He had said he had not been bribed.
links.src_t: CYPRUS: Ex central bank chief gets 5 months for tax fraud (Financial Mirror)

links.detail: Scicluna, governor and former finance minister, pleaded not guilty on 29 May 2024 to fraud and other financial crimes over the government's handling of a private hospital contract (the Vitals concession) while he was finance minister. He stepped aside as governor in July 2024 and was reinstated in July 2025 after the European Central Bank was consulted and raised no objections. These pages don't say how the case stands now.
links.src_t: Maltese governor pleads not guilty to fraud (Central Banking)

links.detail: On 15 September 2017 Spain's National Court decided by majority, on an appeal filed by two trade unions, not to prosecute the former governor over the failure of the commercial bank Bankia in summer 2012. The decision was described as final.
links.src_t: Spanish ex-governor will not face charges over Bankia case (Central Banking)

links.detail: In 2002 a Madrid court sentenced De la Concha to six years in prison for falsifying public documents linked to a securities account of former governor Mariano Rubio that he ran from his office. The report says a company already wound up, NALVI, was used from at least 1986 to hide Rubio as the investor. The ruling could be appealed.
links.src_t: Report on De la Concha's six-year sentence, 4 July 2002 (Diario de León)

links.src_t: Kallas acquitted in $10 million case (Baltic Times)

links.detail: Trichet was charged with spreading false information and publishing inexact accounts of the state-owned bank Crédit Lyonnais for 1991 to mid-1993, and prosecutors recommended a 10-month suspended sentence. In June 2003 judges cleared him, writing that he had only imprecise or incorrect information on the losses. Prosecutors had about 10 days to appeal. The report calls Jacques de Larosière, Banque de France governor at the time, a fellow accused but does not state the verdict for him.
links.src_t: Trichet cleared of wrongdoing (Irish Times)

links.detail: Neary said he would retire early over the regulator's handling of EUR 87 million in secret directors' loans at Anglo Irish Bank. An internal committee found the matter, discovered in January 2008, was not pursued, partly because a letter from Anglo went missing. Neary said he was not told until the finance minister raised it in December 2008.
links.src_t: Financial regulator steps down over Anglo loans inquiry (Irish Times)

links.detail: A central bank official who monitored Snoras bank was sacked in November 2011 and charged with letting Snoras conceal information from the central bank's leadership, including on assets in Swiss banks. A guilty verdict from March 2014 was annulled by a Vilnius court, which found no crime; that ruling can be appealed to the Supreme Court.
links.src_t: Lithuanian court acquits central bank's official who monitored bankrupt Snoras (Lithuania Tribune)

links.detail: The Scheltema committee, set up by finance minister Wouter Bos, reported in June 2010 that De Nederlandsche Bank fell seriously short as supervisor of DSB bank. It missed flaws when licensing DSB in 2005 and was too patient afterwards, though the committee thought a different approach probably would not have prevented DSB's collapse.
links.src_t: Commissie Scheltema: 'DNB schoot tekort bij toezicht op DSB' (Accountant.nl)

links.detail: In 2020 Norges Bank's Supervisory Council warned that the hire of Tangen to run the oil fund could carry a risk of breaking laws, rules and guidelines. It said he still appeared to be the main owner of AKO Capital with voting control, despite the bank saying he had cut those ties, and that the bank had not handled transparency about the applicant list as expected.
links.src_t: Botched hire of oil fund CEO risks breaking the law, say supervisors (IPE)

links.detail: Ruling coalition MPs filed a motion in March 2024 to send Glapiński to the State Tribunal, with eight accusations. They include bond purchases in 2020-2021 said to have indirectly financed the deficit by at least 144 billion zloty, and breaching the bank's political neutrality. A committee adopted its report on 9 October 2026; the Sejm must still decide, and the NBP calls the accusations entirely groundless.
links.src_t: Ruch bez precedensu. Trybunał dla Adama Glapińskiego? Komisja zdecydowała (money.pl)

links.detail: A 600-page report by a committee the Banco de Portugal itself appointed, with technical support from Boston Consulting Group, pointed to failures in its supervision of Banco Espírito Santo going back to the start of the previous decade. Information on the Espírito Santo group and on BES's operations in Angola was reportedly not used. The bank twice refused parliament's request for the report, which was reported by Jornal de Negócios.
links.src_t: Avaliação do Banco de Portugal ao caso BES aponta falhas na supervisão desde Constâncio (Observador)

These are an NGO's reports to the prosecutor; the source reports no charge brought by prosecutors.

links.detail: The National Bank unfroze assets tied to Otar Partskhaladze, a former Prosecutor General sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury, arguing that Georgian citizens cannot be sanctioned without a Georgian court conviction. Three of its four vice presidents and an advisor submitted resignations over the decision. President Salome Zurabishvili criticized acting president Natia Turnava for reportedly changing the rules unilaterally; the source cites no court verdict or official finding.
links.src_t: Top Georgian central bank officials resign over unfreezing of assets of sanctioned former prosecutor (bne IntelliNews)

links.detail: Claim, not confirmed: the Kuwaiti newspaper Al Jarida, citing unnamed sources, reported that the securities regulator had decided to refer Governor Mohammad Al Hashel to prosecutors for suspected breach of investment rules over shares in a local bank. links.detail: The Misrata Criminal Court convicted two people of belonging to an organization set up to seize US$128 million and €5 million from the central bank's Sirte branch in 2013 through coercion. One got 15 years in prison and a LD 2.5 million fine; the other got 13 years and a LD 50,000 fine. The Attorney General's Office reported the ruling in October 2023.
links.src_t: Two convicted for stealing Central Bank of Libya funds worth over US$ 128 million (Libya Herald)

links.detail: Global Witness reported that most Libyan letters of credit enter the international system through ABC International Bank in London, a commercial bank indirectly owned by the central bank and chaired by Governor Saddek Elkaber. It called this a clear conflict of interest, given his authority over letters of credit and anti-money-laundering rules. It built a database of nearly $2.5bn of letters of credit over 13 weeks in 2020 and said sources described mispricing, laundering and procurement fraud; the page reports no official finding of fraud.
links.src_t: Global Witness reveals fraudulent Libyan Letters of Credit money entering international financial system via London (Global Witness)

links.detail: In November 2022 the central bank accused its deputy governor, Ali al-Hibri, of signing forged 50-dinar banknotes it said were printed in Russia and bore his signature, and Governor Saddek Elkaber asked the Attorney-General to pursue a complaint. The bank did not say how many notes were involved. The article gives no response from al-Hibri and no later outcome.
links.src_t: CBL governor files legal complaint against his deputy over forged banknotes (Libya Update)

links.detail: In July 2020 police under the Nouakchott-Ouest prosecutor arrested six people, including one bank employee, over foreign currency taken from the central bank; early reports said about $1 million and later reports $2.4 million, plus $500,000 in counterfeit notes. By March 2021 seven people were in pretrial detention, presumed to have taken about $1 million, and supporters held a sit-in demanding a quick trial. The pages opened report no trial or verdict.
links.src_t: Mauritanie: six présumés voleurs du million de dollars à la Banque centrale arrêtés (Le360 Afrique)

links.detail: In October 2023 the Ministry of Justice said dismissed governor Dieudonné Murengerantwari was being prosecuted for passive corruption, money laundering, misappropriation of public property and undermining the national economy. The prosecutor called this description of the facts provisional, and he was being questioned at the time of the report.
links.src_t: Burundi: Central Bank governor prosecuted for corruption (Africanews)

links.detail: An April 2021 report by Congo's IGF finance inspectorate called a 43 million USD transfer from a central bank account at BGFI Bank to food importer Egal an embezzlement of public funds, and said the bank kept false accounts to cover it. The bank's 2013 accounts showed about 43.1 million USD in that account when the real balance was about 119,000 USD. Mutombo, the bank and PwC did not respond to the journalists who reported this from leaked BGFI documents.
links.src_t: Congo Hold-up : la caisse noire de la Banque centrale du Congo (Seneweb)

links.src_t: DEC arrests money laundering BoZ employee (QFM Zambia)

links.detail: Letters from 2013 presented in a US trial showed the Bank of Mozambique authorized Proindicus to seek a $372 million Credit Suisse loan, later $622 million, and Ematum an $850 million loan, part of the 'hidden debts' of over $2 billion. The letters were signed by board member Silvia de Abreu after a dispatch from governor Ernesto Gove, who in 2016 denied responsibility and said he had never heard of Proindicus. The newssheet Carta de Moçambique reported Gove's suspect status was confirmed and that he may face charges of abuse of office and membership of a criminal organisation.
links.src_t: Bank of Mozambique involved in hidden debts – AIM report (Club of Mozambique)

links.detail: Letters from 2013 presented in a US trial showed the Bank of Mozambique authorized Proindicus to seek a $372 million Credit Suisse loan, later $622 million, and Ematum an $850 million loan, part of the 'hidden debts' of over $2 billion. The letters were signed by board member Silvia de Abreu after a dispatch from governor Ernesto Gove, who in 2016 denied responsibility and said he had never heard of Proindicus. The newssheet Carta de Moçambique reported Gove's suspect status was confirmed and that he may face charges of abuse of office and membership of a criminal organisation.
links.src_t: Bank of Mozambique involved in hidden debts – AIM report (Club of Mozambique)

links.detail: Final findings of Bhutan's Anti-Corruption Commission said a former Deputy Governor of the Royal Monetary Authority allegedly forged official documents, misused power and concealed earnings from World Bank and Asian Development Bank projects. An anonymous informer raised the case in October 2014. The case was forwarded to the Office of the Attorney General; the report gives no later outcome.
links.src_t: RMA's former Deputy Governor allegedly forged official documents and misused power, says ACC findings (BBS)

links.detail: A former currency-exchange employee at the Bank of Korea's Daejeon Sejong-Chungnam headquarters broke the first-in, first-out rule at a coin collector's request, letting 240,000 100-won coins from 2018-2019 be issued before 2017 coins. The collector earned about 180 million won selling the coins and gave the employee about 55 million won. The Daejeon District Court sentenced the employee to 2 years 6 months in prison, a 1 million won fine and confiscation of about 43.31 million won.
links.src_t: "Rare Coins Are Valuable"... Former Bank of Korea Employee Sentenced for Embezzling Coins (Asia Economy)

links.detail: Information on the March Official Cash Rate cut was shared from the bank's media lock-up on 10 March and passed to an economics blogger before the official release. An independent investigation by Deloitte's forensic unit traced the leak to a Newshub Mediaworks reporter. The Reserve Bank ended embargoed lock-ups for news media and analysts.
links.src_t: Reserve Bank takes action after investigation confirms leak (Reserve Bank of New Zealand)

links.detail: A case was brought in 2001 after former governor Rerngchai Marakanond, among other policy-makers, decided to use the central bank's reserves to defend the baht during the Asian financial crisis. On October 5, 2016 Thailand's Supreme Court upheld a lower court's ruling that he had not acted improperly, closing the 15-year case.
links.src_t: Former Bank of Thailand governor cleared of Asian financial crisis charges (Central Banking)

links.detail: A Senior Exchange Control Officer at the National Reserve Bank of Tonga forged a Government bond to support another person's New Zealand visa application and asked for $2,500 pa'anga. She pleaded guilty to forgery, knowingly dealing with forged documents and obtaining money by false pretenses, and her employment was terminated. On May 21, 2019 the Supreme Court of Tonga gave her a two-year sentence, fully suspended, and ordered $800 compensation.
links.src_t: Former Reserve Bank officer gets suspended sentence for serious fraud (Matangi Tonga)

links.detail: Tonga's Anti-Corruption Commissioner sued the bank and its directors, alleging that a 2024 staff payment (for example $6,600 to each of 73 staff) was an unlawful bonus linked to record profit, a breach of trust and misfeasance in public office. The board had described it as a one-off anniversary payout. On 20 November 2025 the Court of Appeal dismissed the proceedings, finding no reasonable cause of action against the bank and that the claim against the directors also failed.
links.src_t: National Reserve Bank of Tonga v Anti-Corruption Commissioner [2025] TOCA 25 (Court of Appeal of Tonga, PacLII)

links.detail: After auditing the Rural Bank of Sapang Dalaga in late 2005, a BSP examiner took consultancy fees from the bank through a third-party firm, collecting P5,000 monthly for a total of P103,500. The court found he used false pretenses and threatened BSP sanctions. The Sandiganbayan denied his appeal and affirmed the guilty verdict, with six years and one month to seven years in prison and perpetual disqualification from public office.
links.src_t: Sandiganbayan upholds conviction of ex-BSP examiner (BusinessWorld)

links.detail: Finance Minister Chris Sinckler fired Governor Delisle Worrell. The government's stated reason was that the board objected to his reported high-handed manner. Some observers believed the reason was his refusal to keep financing the government with new money: his January letter said the government must stop taking new money from the bank to pay its bills. The Appeals Court upheld the minister's right to dismiss him.
links.src_t: Barbados Central Bank governor fired (Caribbean Life)

links.detail: A junta court sentenced former deputy governor Bo Bo Nge to 20 years in prison in December 2022 after a months-long secret trial, sources said for "mismanagement of banks trading foreign currency". The junta-backed Anti-Corruption Commission accused him of not collecting tax on a $5 million Open Society deposit and of placing a $350 million loan in a lower-interest account, with alleged losses of 102, 360 and 655 million kyats. He was arrested on the morning of the February 2021 coup, and economist Sean Turnell called him someone "fighting against corruption".
links.src_t: Myanmar junta sentences former Central Bank official to 20 years in prison (RFA)

links.detail: A 3 July 1996 Ombudsman report found that Governor Samson Ngwele improperly executed ten bank guarantees totalling US$100,000,000, without Board approval and under pressure from Finance Minister Barak Sope, breaching the Reserve Bank Act and the Leadership Code. The guarantees went to Peter Harold Swanson for a 'Trading Programme' that the Ombudsman called a scam, and were still in circulation at the time of the report. The report commended the Governor's later attempts to remedy the situation; he disagreed with its adverse comments about him.
links.src_t: The Provision of Bank Guarantees Given in the Sum of US$100,000,000.00 (Office of the Ombudsman, Vanuatu, via PacLII)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: Governor Ahmed Naseer resigned in July 2019 amid allegations of circumventing the bank's regulations, after being summoned twice by parliament's public finance committee. Former Financial Intelligence Unit head Abdulla Ashraf alleged that Naseer interfered in unit investigations, including one into an MVR 22.5 million deposit to then-President Abdulla Yameen's account shortly before the 2018 election. Naseer denied trying to influence the unit and made counter-allegations against Ashraf; the article reports no charges or findings.
links.src_t: The Edition report on Governor Ahmed Naseer's resignation, 24 July 2019 (The Edition)

links.detail: Claim, not confirmed: the Phnom Penh Post reported that Governor Thor Peng Leath issued a $3 million central bank loan on 31 May 1994 so Credit Bank of Cambodia could meet minimum capital requirements, which central bank officials admitted was 'highly irregular', and that on 8 May 1995 the bank let $145,000 be withdrawn from former commerce minister Var Huot's account after the bank's assets were frozen. Creditors and senior officials claimed preferential treatment; Var Huot said there was none. The article reports no charges or findings against central bank officials.
links.src_t: National Bank tangled in CBC money scandal (Phnom Penh Post)

links.detail: State Comptroller Eliezer Goldberg's report, published 29 April 2002, said former governor Jacob Frenkel unlawfully received hundreds of thousands of shekels when he resigned. It said he demanded and received refunds and payments his predecessors did not get, approved by a senior bank official who reported to him. Goldberg did not say whether the state should demand the money back.

links.detail: Globes reported on 3 February 2009, citing sources, that a draft report by State Comptroller Micha Lindenstrauss found alleged flaws in how the bank's supervision department handled sub-prime investments at Bank Hapoalim, which had written off $1.5 billion on them, and that the bank had only partial information about Israeli banks' exposure to risky instruments. This was a draft: the bank was preparing its reply and said it had responses to all the points.
links.src_t: Regulator faulted on Hapoalim sub-prime investments (Globes)

links.detail: Governor Derick Latibeaudiere borrowed $51 million from the central bank for a house, furnishings and landscaping. At a Public Accounts Committee hearing on 26 May 2009, Auditor General Pamela Monroe Ellis said she had no documents showing the loans were secured and that a $25 million part was still unsecured. The bank's lawyer said $30 million was fully secured against the governor's house, and the committee told both sides to resolve their differences and report back.
links.src_t: After nine months ... Still no proof of collateral from Bank of Jamaica (Jamaica Gleaner)

He was accused of taking bribes worth at least 350,000 zloty to rig tenders between 2001 and 2008, and prosecutors charged the businessmen who ran an IT systems firm with giving him bribes.

On 7 January President Kirchner issued a second decree firing him and accusing him of misconduct. On 8 January the courts suspended both decrees.

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: President Goodluck Jonathan suspended central bank governor Sanusi Lamido Sanusi. The president's aide cited "various acts of financial recklessness". Sanusi had reported the year before that $50bn of oil sold by the state oil company NNPC had not been paid to the government; NNPC repeatedly denied his allegations, and he could not be reached for comment on the suspension.
links.src_t: Nigeria president suspends central bank chief (Al Jazeera)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: Reserve Bank of India governor Urjit Patel resigned, saying only that it was for personal reasons. Media reports said he was annoyed by repeated government efforts to influence central bank policy, after a public spat over alleged interference. Finance Minister Arun Jaitley responded by acknowledging Patel's time at the bank with appreciation.
links.src_t: India's central bank chief quits after spat with government (Dawn)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: Central Bank of Iraq governor Sinan Al Shabibi was removed and a successor named, during a parliamentary probe into possible manipulation of the dinar against the dollar. A committee member said arrest warrants had been issued for 30 people including Al Shabibi and his deputy, Mudher Saleh. The integrity committee chairman said the probe was "not about money, but about procedures"; a finance committee member called it "a political decision and not professional". The article reports no statement from Al Shabibi.
links.src_t: Iraq central bank chief sacked and sought for arrest in currency dispute (The National)

links.detail: The Thai government fired central bank governor Chatu Mongol Sonakul. Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra said he was not satisfied with the bank's policy of keeping interest rates low. The readable part of the article, which is cut off by a paywall, carries no response from the governor.
links.src_t: Thai government sacks central bank boss (Central Banking)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: Central Bank of Cyprus governor Panicos Demetriades resigned, to leave on 10 April, with no reason given. The president had earlier said he would begin proceedings to have him removed for not doing his job properly; at the resignation a government statement thanked him for helping prevent the country's bankruptcy. The article carries no statement from Demetriades on the dispute.
links.src_t: Cyprus central bank governor resigns amid simmering dispute with president (Fox News)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: Iran replaced central bank governor Valiollah Seif, in post since August 2013, with Abdolnasser Hemati. The article gives no stated reason for the removal: President Hassan Rouhani thanked Seif for his "strong and serious service" and said a key priority was tackling "illegal credit institutions". It records no statement from Seif.
links.src_t: Iran sacks central bank chief, as rial's slide continues (The New Arab)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: Bank Indonesia governor Syahril was released after six months of detention when prosecutors' detention orders expired. He still faced corruption charges and a possible life sentence over his alleged involvement in the 546 billion rupiah Bank Bali scandal, while the administration was pushing to remove him and install its own candidates. A presidential spokesman said "This release merely follows legal procedures". A Jakarta court later sentenced him to three years in 2002, and in 2004 Kyodo, quoting a senior Supreme Court judge, reported the top court had rejected prosecutors' appeal and acquitted him on all charges (Central Banking, 1 Oct 2004: centralbanking.com/node/1411040).
links.src_t: Syahril back at helm of central bank (The Straits Times, via Asia Pacific Solidarity Network)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: President Joyce Banda removed Reserve Bank of Malawi governor Perks Ligoya, according to two unnamed sources, with Charles Chuka reportedly chosen to succeed him. No official reason was stated; the reporter described it as her latest move to clean house and woo donors back. No one at the central bank was available for comment.
links.src_t: New Malawi president sacks central bank chief (Nampa-Reuters, The Namibian)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: Sierra Leone's recently elected president dismissed the governor of the central bank, and Kelfala Kallon was appointed on 15 August as the bank's third governor in 17 months. The readable part of the article, cut off by a paywall, does not name the dismissed governor or give either side's reason.
links.src_t: Sierra Leone's president fires governor and appoints successor (Central Banking)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: President Bio sent Bank of Sierra Leone governor Kelfala Kallon on "indefinite leave" and named deputy Ibrahim Stevens interim head. The advisory firm that wrote this article reports no official reason and no response from Kallon; it says the president tried to bypass the 2019 Bank of Sierra Leone Act, under which sacking the governor needs a two-thirds majority in parliament.
links.src_t: Sierra Leone's central bank governor removed months to elections (Songhai Advisory)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: President Nicolas Maduro announced the firing of Central Bank chief Nelson Merentes, who the article says handed in his resignation, and named economist Ricardo Sanguino to succeed him. The article reports no reason from Maduro and no statement from Merentes; it places the firing amid an economic crisis and a bungled release of larger banknotes.
links.src_t: Maduro sacks the head of Venezuela's central bank (PTI, Business Standard)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: Parliament voted no confidence in National Bank of Ukraine head Volodymyr Stelmakh, with 227 of 450 seats in favour. Parliament cited a fall of nearly half in the hryvna's value since November, a shrinking economy and rising deficits. President Yushchenko's office called the decision "illegal" and repeated its support for Stelmakh.
links.src_t: Ukraine president says sacking of national bank boss illegal (UNIAN)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: The Hungarian cabinet decided to go ahead with a draft bill cutting National Bank governor András Simor's monthly pay by 75%, from about Ft 8 million to Ft 2 million, through a cap on everyone paid from public funds. A government spokesman said this did not threaten the bank's independence because it applied to the whole public sector. The ECB said such changes should apply only to future appointments and be made in consultation with the bank. The article has no statement from Simor.
links.src_t: Hungarian Cabinet Rejects ECB Warning Over MNB Pay Cuts (Hungary Around the Clock, via XpatLoop)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: President Moncef Marzouki fired central bank governor Mustapha Kamel Nabli, alleging he had refused to bring monetary policy in line with the country's economic needs. The elected assembly approved the move in July 2012. The article carries no statement from Nabli.
links.src_t: Tunisia assembly backs central bank head firing (AP, Washington Examiner)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: Central Bank of Belize governor Gustavo Manuel Vasquez lost his post. Prime Minister John Briceño said the board recommended he resign because of "a lot of policy differences". Vasquez wrote that his appointment was terminated on the instructions of the Ministry of Finance, that he faced opposition from it, and that he had tried to restore the bank's integrity and operational autonomy.

links.role: Paid a former official for speeches or advice
links.detail: Janet Yellen (Fed chair until early 2018): from Federal Reserve to paid speeches for financial firms named in her disclosures. CNN reports that Yellen's financial disclosures, filed ahead of her Treasury confirmation, show she made more than $7 million from speeches in recent years, including $952,200 from Citigroup. Other firms listed include PIMCO, Barclays, Citadel, BNP Paribas, UBS, Credit Suisse, ING, Standard Chartered and City National Bank; CNN also names Google, Goldman Sachs, Bank of America and Salesforce. She pledged to seek written authorization before taking part in matters related to Barclays, Citi, Citadel, Credit Suisse and Goldman Sachs.

Prasarn was unavailable for comment. Korn Chatikavanij said Kittiratt should not have spoken out, as it could erode investor confidence.
links.src_t: Kittiratt wants central bank chief replaced (Bangkok Post)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials

Co-author Tamaz Mechiauri reportedly argued that the National Bank board's composition was against the current leadership's interests and that the change would discourage currency speculation. Bidzina Ivanishvili blamed the bank and its chairman Giorgi Kadagidze for the lari's fall; the article carries no statement from Kadagidze.

links.detail: The Daily Graphic reported the government was pushing for the exit of Bank of Ghana second deputy governor Johnson Asiama. His counsel alleged that some government officials had told him they wanted him to step aside; Asiama said he had not resigned. The article reports no official government reason and no final outcome.

He said Addison had borrowed "in excess of 7billion dollars" on the bank's balance sheet to support the cedi and claimed the government had borrowed illegally through the bank. The article reports no answer from the governor or the government.

Wampah said he had agreed with President Mahama to leave at the end of March, ahead of his August term end, so a successor could settle in before the elections. The article reports no government response.
links.src_t: BoG Governor was forced to resign - MP (Daily Post)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: In a speech announcing the 2017 budget, President Rodrigo Duterte told the central bank governor Amando Tetangco "I will give you a whack" and threatened criminal charges against the Anti-Money Laundering Council, which Tetangco chairs, accusing it of not tracking drug money, without details on the alleged corruption. Tetangco did not immediately respond; Deputy Governor Diwa Guinigundo said the bank was independent.
links.src_t: Philippines' Duterte wants to give bank Governor 'a whack', charge staff (Daily FT)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: Governor Arjuna Mahendran's term ended on 30 June; he told the Monetary Board he would not seek reappointment until the parliamentary committee COPE finished its Treasury bond probe. President Maithripala Sirisena, who said in June 2015 that Mahendran should resign, tweeted he would appoint a new governor within hours, while Prime Minister Ranil Wickremesinghe said Mahendran could not be removed because the charges "had never been proved". The Auditor General found a Rs. 1.6 billion loss; no new governor was announced that day.
links.src_t: Political tug-o-war over CB Governor (Daily FT)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: La Paz prosecutors ordered the arrest of former Banco Central president Edwin Rojas and three former executives, investigated for breach of duties and uneconomic conduct over a 2024 regulation that the prosecutor says allowed irregular sovereign bond transactions, with alleged damage of $us 124 million. Rojas invoked his right to silence. The article does not say whether they have been formally charged.
links.src_t: Aprehenden al expresidente y tres exejecutivos del Banco Central (Los Tiempos)

links.detail: State Bank of Pakistan governor Yaseen Anwar resigned. The Finance Ministry spokesman said he cited personal reasons; unnamed senior officials said that was a cover for differences with Finance Minister Ishaq Dar over inflation and reserves, and that he was unhappy with a recent deputy governor appointment. The article reports no government pressure.
links.src_t: State Bank governor resigns, cites personal reasons (Dawn)

links.detail: Parliament approved the resignation letter of National Bank head Kubanychbek Bokontaev, in post since 2021, relieving him ahead of schedule. The article gives no reason from either side.
links.src_t: Parliament of Kyrgyzstan relieves head of National Bank of his post (24.kg)

links.detail: President Néstor Kirchner's government was to replace central bank president Alfonso Prat-Gay, whose term ended that week, with Martin Redrado, subject to Senate approval. The article says the trigger was unclear; local media suggested disagreements over the debt restructuring. Neither side is quoted.
links.src_t: Argentine Central Bank chiefs to go (MercoPress)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: A bill expected to pass on July 15 would place the National Bank of Serbia under government control and allow the dismissal of governor Mladjan Dinkic. The article reports the government side's complaints: Prime Minister Zoran Djindjic wanted a devaluation Dinkic resisted, and DOS members said a party official cannot be governor. Dinkic said the law would make the bank dependent on government and parliament; authorities said his claims had no foundation.
links.src_t: Serbia: central bank bill and Dinkic (IWPR)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: Bangladesh Bank governor Atiur Rahman resigned after an $81m hack, saying he was "ready to resign from my post for the sake of the country". He had been criticised for not telling the finance minister about the loss, and Finance Minister Abul Maal Abdul Muhith called the bank's handling very incompetent. The article does not say the government asked him to go.
links.src_t: Bangladesh Bank governor resigns after $81m hack (Al Jazeera)

links.detail: During the Asian Financial Crisis, Bank Negara governor Ahmad Mohd Don and deputy Fong Weng Phak resigned "as a matter of principle". The article says Ahmad Don favoured tight monetary policy, backed by Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim, while Mahathir and Daim Zainuddin wanted an expansionary approach, and that Anwar was sacked over the dispute.
links.src_t: History of BNM governors who resigned in the past (Loanstreet)

links.detail: President Boris Yeltsin fired Central Bank chairman Viktor Gerashchenko for his role in the Black Tuesday ruble crash and appointed Tatyana Paramonova. The State Duma then rejected her in a secret ballot, 107 to 127; opponents said the constitution barred hiring or firing the bank's chief without Duma approval.

links.detail: Asharq Al-Awsat reported in November 2020 that Bahrain's High Criminal Court fined the Central Bank of Iran and other Iran-owned banks, including Future Bank, BD 1 million each, and jailed three Future Bank officials for five years. Prosecutors said the Central Bank of Iran planned to launder billions of dollars through Future Bank, which handled suspicious SWIFT transfers favoring Iranian entities, mainly the central bank, without reporting them.
links.src_t: Bahraini Court Fines Central Bank of Iran in Money Laundering Case (Asharq Al-Awsat)

links.detail: On 18 January 2018 a court in Côte d'Ivoire, with judge Sombé Méïté giving the verdict, sentenced Gbagbo, Aké N'Gbo, Katinan and Dallo to 20 years in prison and a 329 billion CFA franc fine for offences including group theft by break-in of BCEAO vaults and cash during the December 2010 to April 2011 post-election crisis. Seven bailiffs got 36 months and a 700,000 CFA franc fine. Katinan was absent throughout the trial. Gbagbo always denied the charges, and on 6 August 2022 President Ouattara pardoned him.
links.src_t: Braquage BCEAO: Gbagbo et 3 de ses ex-ministres condamnés à 20 ans de prison et 329 milliards FCFA d'amende (Abidjan.net, citing APA)

links.detail: A summit of UEMOA heads of state accepted governor Dacoury-Tabley's resignation in January 2011. He was criticized for ignoring a 23 December decision by UEMOA finance ministers that gave Alassane Ouattara power over the institution, and the article says the BCEAO paid out 60 to 100 billion CFA francs to the Gbagbo regime after that date. Senegal's President Abdoulaye Wade asked for an audit and alleged that the former governor moved 500 billion CFA francs to Gbagbo after being dismissed; another figure cited is 300 billion, and that report gives no audit result.
links.src_t: BCEAO: démission du gouverneur Dacoury, un proche de l'ancien président Gbagbo (Connectionivoirienne, with Nettali.net)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: A woman arrested on 17 October 2019 was implicated with others including former president Ian Khama and former intelligence head Isaac Kgosi in allegedly stealing P100 billion from Bank of Botswana. High Court Judge Zein Kebonang discharged and acquitted her of unexplained property and a false passport declaration, the state withdrew a terrorism financing charge, and he found the accusations fabricated. He referred the investigator to police for perjury prosecution.
links.src_t: Butterfly walks free (The Patriot on Sunday)

links.detail: Governor Kallon told Parliament on 22 November 2021 that he "bribed" people hoarding the Leone to bring it back into the banking system. The Anti-Corruption Commission investigated and said in May 2022 that he was referring to cash swap operations in which the bank sold about US$68.6 million in foreign currency in 2021, that the word was used in error, and that it had closed the investigation after advising him to choose his words more carefully.
links.src_t: ACC concludes investigation of "bribe" statement by the governor of bank of Sierra Leone (Sierra Leone Telegraph)

links.detail: La Nación reported on 17 April 2026 that the BCRA is examining a circuit that moved at least US$900 million between January 2022 and October 2023, in which dollars bought at the official rate allegedly ended up in the parallel market through exchange houses. The BCRA opened procedures against officials over its ethics rules, after raids at the bank that followed reports from the UIF and Procelac. The companies deny wrongdoing.
links.src_t: El Banco Central investiga operaciones irregulares por US$900 millones durante el último gobierno (La Nación)

links.detail: In March 2019 police summoned Maldives Monetary Authority governor Ahmed Naseer and confirmed he was being investigated for obstruction of justice. Parliament's Financial Committee had questioned him on 5 March about the Anti-Corruption Commission report on the embezzlement case at the Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation and about the removal of Abdulla Ashraf as head of the Financial Intelligence Unit. The report names no charge or court outcome.
links.src_t: Governor of Maldives Monetary Authority summoned by police (Edition.mv)

links.detail: The Banco de Portugal's ethics committee examined a request by governor Carlos Costa to be excused from matters concerning Caixa Geral de Depositos, discussed at a meeting in April 2019 after an EY audit of CGD's management. Costa had been a CGD board member from 2004 to 2006 and may have sat on extended credit council meetings that approved operations which caused losses, while now heading the supervisor assessing former CGD directors. Vice-governor Elisa Ferreira did not recuse herself but told the committee of a possible conflict of interest relating to her husband's past role at La Seda. The committee's conclusions were not made public. No conclusion was published.
links.src_t: Comissao de etica do Banco de Portugal analisou escusa do governador na Caixa (Observador)

links.detail: In February 2020 the Prosecutor General's Office charged Ibrahim Athif Shakoor, former head of the Financial Intelligence Unit at the Maldives Monetary Authority, with negligence and failing to act appropriately on the MMPRC case, in which state funds were moved to private accounts. At a preliminary hearing at the Criminal Court in September 2020 he asked the Prosecutor General's Office to arrange a confessional agreement waiving prison in exchange for admitting a breach of the money laundering and terrorism financing law. He said he had told the then MMA governor, Azeema Adam, about illegal MMPRC transactions at least four times and had also tried to alert police; he denied the allegations at an August 2019 Public Finance Committee meeting. Atoll Times reported on 14 October 2025 that the Prosecutor General’s Office withdrew the charge, saying it qualified for an advisory agreement and citing how long the case had been in court. No conviction is reported.
links.src_t: Athif seeks confessional agreement in MMPRC-linked case (Edition.mv)

links.detail: The Direccion de Persecucion de la Corrupcion Administrativa brought former Banco Central governor Jose Lois Malkun, former deputy governor Felix Calvo, former administrative director Cesar Apolinar Veloz and former legal counsel Manuel Rubio Cristoforis to court on charges including breach of trust (abuso de confianza) and criminal association, over the disappearance of 18 promissory notes worth RD$10,663 million said to have been handed fraudulently to former banker Manuel Arturo Pellerano. The Banco Central neither filed a complaint nor joined as a civil party; a Junta Monetaria resolution signed by legal counsel Olga Morel said the bank's authorities were negotiating the return of the notes with Pellerano.
links.src_t: Bancentral no se querella contra tres ex funcionarios (El Dia)

links.detail: The Kisutu Resident Magistrate's Court in Dar es Salaam sentenced businessmen Farijala Hussein and Rajabu Maranda to five years in prison, finding them guilty of offences related to financial impropriety, forgery and obtaining credit under false pretences, and ordered them to return the money they had taken. The report, published 27 May 2011, describes these as the first court cases heard after the 2008 Bank of Tanzania corruption scandal. No amount is given.
links.src_t: Tanzania jails two over central bank corruption scandal (Central Banking)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: The commission of enquiry into the collapse of CL Financial and the Hindu Credit Union, run by sole commissioner Sir Anthony Colman and commissioned in November 2010, found the Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago's powers of regulatory control over the insurance industry to be 'fundamentally deficient', tracing this to the Insurance Act's inadequate regulatory scope. The report said the Inspector of financial institutions tried to use the limited tools then available but that Clico and CL Financial management largely ignored them, and that had some powers in an unenacted Insurance Bill been in force by 2008 the collapse might have been avoided. It blamed no named Central Bank official. The enquiry sat from March 2011 to May 2013 at an estimated cost of $36.2 million, including a $7 million fee for Colman.
links.src_t: Colman report knocks T&T Central Bank in Clico, HCU fiasco (Stabroek News)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: The Central Bank of Eswatini rejected Farmers Bank's commercial banking licence application in late 2017, then granted it after a royal command in September 2018. Governor Majozi Sithole said he was given a royal command to attend a 14 July 2017 meeting about the bank, and in May 2018 finance minister Martin Dlamini told the central bank the king had ordered an investigation into its reluctance to license it. The central bank revoked the licence on 5 October 2020 over the unexplained source of the seed capital, commerce minister Manqoba Khumalo ruled in December 2020 that the bank should keep it, and the central bank reinstated it in January 2021 while objecting to procedural improprieties.
links.src_t: The central bank in a tiny African country tried to block a suspicious banking venture. Then the king's allies intervened. (ICIJ, Swazi Secrets)

links.detail: In June 2015 the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority said it would commission an internal review of the involvement of local people and financial institutions in the FIFA corruption case, after Caymanian businessman Jeffrey Webb was arrested in Switzerland on 27 May. Managing director Cindy Scotland's husband, former minister Mark Scotland, had worked for the Cayman Islands Football Association under Webb and was with Webb at the arrest, and Gloria Glidden, deputy head of the authority's banking division, is the wife of former minister Cline Glidden, who was also in Switzerland with Webb. Chairman George McCarthy said Scotland would remain managing director and that there was no evidence any Cayman bank had done anything wrong.
links.src_t: Cayman's financial regulator begins internal review (Cayman Compass)

links.role: Received money, favors or contracts from the bank
links.detail: In March 2022 someone posing as the chief financial officer of the US firm RVK emailed the Banco Central de Chile a false invoice for US$205,000 from an address differing from the real one by one letter, then asked for payment to a new account at another bank, and the bank paid. The bank filed a complaint with the Ministerio Publico in May 2022 and dismissed the head of its accounting management department on 23 June 2022 as an administrative sanction for the erroneous payment; he sued in the First Labour Court of Santiago in December, calling the dismissal abusive and unfair and seeking 267 million pesos. The bank said there was no indication that any official took part deliberately.
links.src_t: Banco Central demandado por 267 millones por despido en caso de suplantacion y fraude (Meganoticias)

links.detail: On 6 June 2006 a sentencing court in Asuncion presided by Sandra Farias, with Gustavo Amarilla and Miguel Said, sentenced former president Luis Gonzalez Macchi to six years in prison for lesion de confianza as alleged instigator of the diversion of US$16 million to the United States from two private banks, Union and Orienta, which the Banco Central intervened in and declared bankrupt. The report states that Jose Pecci, former superintendent of the institute emisor, was sentenced to eight years, without explaining his role. Gonzalez Macchi said he would appeal; prosecutor Victoria Acuna had sought ten years. An appeals court later cleared Gonzalez Macchi, saying the evidence was insufficient; that ruling is recorded separately here.
links.src_t: Condenan a seis anos de carcel al ex presidente de Paraguay (Notife)

links.detail: An Anti-Corruption Commission report publicised in February 2019 found the Maldives Monetary Authority negligent in the MMPRC case, in which MVR 1.3 billion was embezzled from Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation. The commission found the authority's Financial Intelligence Unit was told in 2014 of a US$59 million cheque from MMPRC to the company SOF but did not investigate it properly, did not examine large SOF transactions through Bank of Maldives and Bank of Ceylon, and did not forward suspected money-laundering cases to the relevant authorities. Former FIU head Ibrahim Athif Shakoor said governor Azeema Adam objected to filing a police report, citing insufficient FIU staff and resources; Azeema said she had told the FIU head to investigate SOF's transactions and gave no specific instructions because the FIU decided its own actions.
links.src_t: ACC finds MMA negligent in MMPRC scandal (Edition.mv)

links.role: Pressured, dismissed or prosecuted bank officials
links.detail: Testifying as a witness at the Maputo City Court on 23 November 2021 in the hidden debts trial of 19 people, former Bank of Mozambique governor Ernesto Gove said he signed authorisations for foreign loans to Proindicus, Ematum and MAM on grounds of sovereignty and national security, and admitted irregularities in how the central bank granted them, including that the requests were handed personally to senior bank officials by Eugenio Matlaba and Antonio Carlos do Rosario rather than submitted at a counter, and that the financing contracts with Credit Suisse had already been signed. Article 83 of the Foreign Exchange Law regulations bars the central bank from authorising foreign loans to private companies whose repayment depends on a state guarantee; Gove argued it applied only to guarantees obtained after loans were agreed, and judge Efigenio Baptista rejected that reading. The loans exceeded two billion US dollars, from Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia.
links.src_t: Hidden debts trial: Illegal loans were in interests of 'sovereignty', claims ex-governor of Bank of Mozambique (Club of Mozambique / AIM)

links.detail: In August 2020 Norges Bank's Executive Board revised incoming NBIM chief executive Nicolai Tangen's employment terms to reduce conflict-of-interest concerns raised by the Storting's Standing Committee on Finance and Economic Affairs: Tangen would divest his holding in AKO Capital LLP and transfer his holding and dividend rights to the charitable AKO Foundation, with no ownership interest in AKO Capital in perpetuity, and would hold all his personal fund assets as bank deposits. Supervisory Board chair Julie Brodtkorb said there had been a breach of guidelines, regulations and laws in Tangen's appointment. Executive Board chair Oystein Olsen said the board had believed the existing contractual framework was sufficient but acknowledged the Storting took a different view. Tangen could take office on 1 September.
links.src_t: NBIM revises Nicolai Tangen terms following conflict of interest concerns (European Pensions)

links.detail: ADDS TURNAVA'S OWN ACCOUNT. At a briefing on 20 September 2023, acting National Bank of Georgia president Natia Turnava confirmed she had single-handedly adopted a change to the procedure for executing sanctions regimes, made on 19 September and effective 20 September 2023, saying it fell within the discretion of the bank's president and that she had informed National Bank Council members in advance. TBC Bank and Bank of Georgia had frozen the accounts of Otar Partskhaladze; Turnava said the banks did not violate the law because the amendment took effect the day of her briefing. Vice-president Papuna Lezhava resigned, for reasons the report says are unknown.
links.src_t: Turnava confirms that she single-handedly changed the procedure for implementing the sanctions regimes (GBC)

links.detail: On the 49th day of the trial, 23 November 2021, Banco de Mocambique administrator Silvina de Abreu testified that under normal conditions the central bank should not have authorised the ProIndicus, EMATUM and MAM loans, because the Foreign Exchange Law bars approving loans whose disbursement depends on a State guarantee. She said then governor Ernesto Gove told her to work only with the management group and not to involve technical staff, as the file concerned state security and sovereignty. The approvals she described were US$372 million for ProIndicus in March 2013, US$850 million for EMATUM in August 2013 and a further US$250 million sought for ProIndicus less than three months later.
links.src_t: 49o dia do julgamento do escandalo das 'dividas ocultas': Banco de Mocambique nao deveria ter autorizado emprestimos da ProIndicus, EMATUM e MAM (CDD Mocambique trial-monitoring bulletin, Year 03 No. 255)

links.detail: A former Bank of Korea employee, moved in 2013 to the museum operations team and responsible for paying in the proceeds of Bank of Korea publication sales, diverted about 56 million won in 14 transfers to a personal account and used a Bank of Korea corporate card to buy about 12 million won of commemorative uncut banknote sheets. The Seoul Central District Court, Judge Lee Heung-kwon presiding, convicted the employee of occupational breach of trust and embezzlement and imposed eight months in prison suspended for two years, noting the full amount had been repaid.
links.src_t: Naratdon ppaedollin jeon Haneun jigwon jiphaengyuye 2nyeon seongo (Saturday Economy / sateconomy.co.kr)

links.detail: The Gambian government's White Paper on the Commission of Inquiry into former president Yahya Jammeh's financial dealings accepted the finding that between September 2015 and January 2017 General Sulayman Badjie, purportedly acting for Jammeh, issued instructions to the Governor of the Central Bank or his deputies for withdrawals of US dollars, and that cash was handed over by the Governor to soldiers and loaded into vehicles. The Commission held Badjie accountable for illegal withdrawals of $15,785,601, 300,000 euros and D9,606,000, and the government ordered the money recovered through forfeiture and sale of his properties. The document also records $28.5 million illegally granted in the CBG 3M Account in 2000-2001 and $268,000 of money stolen from the Central Bank used to buy the Observer Newspaper.
links.src_t: Government White Paper on the Report of the Commission of Inquiry into the financial dealings of former President Yahya Jammeh (Ministry of Justice, The Gambia)

links.detail: A Global Witness investigation published on 19 February 2021 found that senior Central Bank of Libya officials hold paid overseas directorships, and that Governor Saddek Elkaber chairs a London-based bank indirectly owned by the Central Bank of Libya, which the report calls a conflict of interest. The report also said the bank's letters of credit data point to ongoing financial crime in the system, citing nearly $2.5bn of private sector letters of credit approved between April and July 2020 and a $110m letter of credit for power equipment diverted to a UAE company with a near identical name to the original contractor. The report states it makes no allegation that any individual or bank broke the law.
links.src_t: Discredited (Global Witness)

links.detail: Warsaw's District Prosecutor's Office is investigating the disclosure of information classified as 'secret' from the closed part of the Monetary Policy Council meeting of 8 September 2023, after a complaint by one of the Council's members. On 12 June 2025 prosecutors secured documents at the National Bank of Poland's head office, after the bank had twice refused to hand them over; a court had earlier overturned a decision refusing to open the investigation.

links.detail: At the trial reported in March 2020, prosecutors charged Feliks Kasperovich, together with Andrei Podgorny of the National Bank's information technology directorate, with taking bribes of at least $868,750, starting with $10,000 in 2007 and including $260,000 paid in 2016. Igor Kudasov, head of the bank's payment systems directorate, was charged with taking a $30,000 bribe and had been held in custody since 29 December 2018. Kasperovich admitted the charges in full. This is the trial stage of the computer-supply bribery network reported in 2016.

links.detail: A State Comptroller's report, reported on 17 October 2012, found faults in how the Bank of Israel managed foreign currency reserves that had grown from USD 28 billion to USD 75 billion since March 2008. It said supervision and control of the Market Operations Division were deficient, there was no control over the receipt of bids, handling of possible employee conflicts of interest was incomplete, and the two committees chaired by the Governor worked without written procedures. The Bank said some issues were corrected during the audit and others were being addressed.
links.src_t: State Comptroller report on Bank of Israel foreign currency reserves management (Globes)

links.detail: In 2017 a Central Bank of Eswatini evaluations team recommended the board reject a commercial banking licence for Farmers Bank, warning it would tarnish the integrity of the bank's licensing policy, but a conditional licence was issued in September 2018 after a royal command from King Mswati III. The central bank revoked the licence in October 2020 because the bank could not prove the origin of its seed capital; an appeal chaired by commerce minister Manqoba Khumalo reinstated it in January 2021. A 2022 report by Kroll, commissioned by the central bank, said it was likely that third parties outside the bank intervened in the process and instructed it to proceed, and that R89m of seed capital had been used from 2019 to buy silver bullion the central bank could not verify existed.
links.src_t: Swazi Secrets part 3: How to capture a bank (Financial Mail / amaBhungane and Finance Uncovered)

links.detail: Former Central Bank of Cyprus governor Christodoulos Christodoulou and co-defendants faced 29 charges over a 1 million euro payment said to have been made so he would overlook Andreas Vgenopoulos's acquisition of a controlling stake in Laiki Bank, which failed in 2013. The first charge covers February to November 2006, when he was governor, and alleges he agreed to take 1 million euros from Vgenopoulos and Marfin Investment Group. He is also accused of failing to investigate whether MIG could control Laiki after it bought 9.98% of shares from Marfin Financial Group and 8.18% from the TOSCA fund on 6 February 2006 without central bank approval, and of two counts of abuse of authority; all defendants faced money laundering charges. Christodoulou said the money was an advance for ten years of consultancy; in October 2014 he pleaded guilty to tax evasion and was jailed for five months. The case was expected to go to the Nicosia criminal court at the end of September 2016; the report gives no verdict.
links.src_t: Christodoulou faces 29 charges over Laiki payment (Cyprus Mail)

links.detail: Deloitte, engaged by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand on 11 March 2016 and reporting on 12 April 2016, found the source of the leak of the 10 March 2016 Official Cash Rate decision was a Mediaworks employee. A Mediaworks journalist in the media lockup emailed a draft story out of the lockup room without RBNZ approval shortly before 8am; another Mediaworks employee who overheard colleagues discussing the rate drop emailed Michael Reddell at 8.04am, ahead of the 9am announcement, and Reddell did not notify the RBNZ until 9.08am. Mediaworks self-reported on 5 April 2016. Deloitte judged the Minister of Finance's office unlikely to be the source.
links.src_t: Report on the investigation into the OCR leak (Deloitte, for the Reserve Bank of New Zealand)

links.detail: The Central Bank of Kenya awarded the contract to print new-look currency (Sh18 billion) to De La Rue International, which operates the Ruaraka plant co-owned by the Kenyan government; De La Rue beat Giesecke & Devrient, Crane Currency and Oberthur Fiduciaire. Crane AB disputed the award before the procurement review board.

links.detail: Sveriges Riksbank signed an agreement with De La Rue (announced 19 September 2018) to print Swedish banknotes for just over three years, replacing Crane.
links.src_t: Central Banking: De La Rue beats European competition to Swedish banknote contract

links.detail: Danmarks Nationalbank selected Oberthur Fiduciaire as its new banknote supplier under a four-year framework, first notes in circulation in 2020.
links.src_t: Central Banking: Denmark selects Oberthur Fiduciaire as banknote supplier

links.detail: Oberthur Fiduciaire won a Deutsche Bundesbank tender to print part of the euro banknotes for 2013, after an earlier award (about two years before) that losing bidders had challenged unsuccessfully.
links.src_t: Heuking Kühn Lüer Wojtek: Oberthur successful on Bundesbank bid

links.detail: The Centrale Bank van Curaçao en Sint Maarten contracted Crane Currency to produce the new Caribbean guilder banknotes (and the Royal Canadian Mint for coins). The release says Crane is headquartered in Massachusetts with plants in Malta and Sweden and supplies more than 50 central banks.
links.src_t: Curaçao Chronicle: Crane Currency and the Royal Canadian Mint to supply Caribbean Guilder currency

links.detail: The CBCS announcement states Crane has supplied banknotes, banknote paper and anti-counterfeiting features for the central bank of Mexico (a client list in a third-party announcement, not a contract notice).
links.src_t: Curaçao Chronicle: Crane Currency and the Royal Canadian Mint to supply Caribbean Guilder currency

links.detail: The CBCS announcement states Crane has supplied banknotes, banknote paper and anti-counterfeiting features for the central bank of Guyana (a client list in a third-party announcement, not a contract notice).
links.src_t: Curaçao Chronicle: Crane Currency and the Royal Canadian Mint to supply Caribbean Guilder currency

links.detail: The CBCS announcement states Crane has supplied the new banknotes of Aruba in 2019 (a client list in a third-party announcement, not a contract notice).
links.src_t: Curaçao Chronicle: Crane Currency and the Royal Canadian Mint to supply Caribbean Guilder currency

links.detail: Crane has supplied banknote paper and security features to the US Treasury Department since 1879 (the customer is the Treasury, not the Federal Reserve).
links.src_t: Curaçao Chronicle: Crane Currency and the Royal Canadian Mint to supply Caribbean Guilder currency

links.detail: Crane printed Liberian dollar banknotes for the Central Bank of Liberia under two contracts totalling L$15 billion at a cost of US$15,331,689.20.
links.src_t: FrontPage Africa: Crane Currency Refutes Wrong Doing in L$16 Billion Saga

links.role: Bribery or misconduct with the bank
links.detail: Liberia's Presidential Investigation Team alleged Crane conspired with CBL officials to print L$18,151,000,000, beyond the contracted L$15 billion. Crane denied wrongdoing and kickbacks and said it had not been charged; the PIT report also named former CBL Governor Charles Sirleaf. This is an allegation, not a finding by a court.
links.src_t: FrontPage Africa: Crane Currency Refutes Wrong Doing in L$16 Billion Saga

links.detail: Goznak (Russian state printer) printed Libyan dinars for the parallel eastern Central Bank (Benghazi/Bayda), which is not internationally recognized; Reuters-cited Russian customs data showed 4.5 billion dinars shipped Feb-June 2019. Malta seized two containers on 1 November 2019, citing UN resolutions that recognize only the Tripoli government.
links.src_t: Middle East Institute (Jonathan M. Winer): Seized Russian-printed dinars...

links.detail: The MEI article states that the regular Libyan dinar notes are printed by Britain's De La Rue.
links.src_t: Middle East Institute (Jonathan M. Winer): Seized Russian-printed dinars...

links.detail: G+D suspended all deliveries to Myanmar's state-owned Security Print Works after the military crackdown; before that it supplied raw materials, supplies and system components for printing kyat banknotes. G+D is headquartered in Munich. (The customer named is the state printer, not the Central Bank of Myanmar; press release undated on the fetched page, issued 2021.)
links.src_t: G+D press release: Giesecke+Devrient suspends deliveries to state security printer in Myanmar

links.role: Bribery or misconduct with the bank
links.detail: The UK Serious Fraud Office opened an investigation into De La Rue in July 2019 over suspected corruption in South Sudan (South Sudan awarded it a 2011 contract for 2.8 billion banknotes) and closed it in June 2020, saying the case did not meet the test for prosecution.
links.src_t: City A.M.: SFO ends corruption probe into banknote printer De La Rue

links.detail: South Sudan awarded De La Rue a contract to produce 2.8 billion banknotes in 2011, and new notes including 500-pound notes were printed by De La Rue in 2019.
links.src_t: Eye Radio: Case dropped against S.Sudan banknotes, passports printing firm

links.role: Bribery or misconduct with the bank
links.detail: De La Rue said in September 2010 that some employees had deliberately falsified banknote paper specification test certificates for a limited number of customers; Eye Radio reports this was followed by suspension of supply to the Reserve Bank of India (customer link per Eye Radio).
links.src_t: Central Banking: De La Rue says staff falsified banknote tests; Eye Radio (2020)

links.role: Bribery or misconduct with the bank
links.detail: Securency International (now CCL Secure) pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria to conspiracy to provide benefits to foreign public officials to obtain business with the note-issuing authority of this country (December 1999 - February 2001). Securency paid a pecuniary penalty of A$19,809,772 and NPA A$1,856,710. NPA is wholly owned by the Reserve Bank of Australia; Securency was a 50-50 RBA-Innovia joint venture. (Pleas and penalties listed under 2011 entries of the RBA chronology.)

links.detail: At the EFCC trial of former CBN Governor Godwin Emefiele over alleged unlawful printing of redesigned naira notes (2022), a prosecution witness said original naira designs were historically handled by De La Rue, while the new notes were printed locally.
links.src_t: BusinessDay: Witness alleges Emefiele breached CBN Act in naira redesign trial

links.detail: NSPMC printed the redesigned 2022 naira notes; the EFCC verified CBN payments to NSPMC as part of its four-count prosecution of former CBN Governor Godwin Emefiele for alleged unlawful printing of new notes (charges, not a conviction).
links.src_t: BusinessDay: Witness alleges Emefiele breached CBN Act in naira redesign trial

links.detail: Investment Management Agreement dated June 29, 2020 between Corporate Credit Facilities LLC (formed by the New York Fed) and BlackRock Financial Management, Inc. as manager of the Primary Market Corporate Credit Facility (PMCCF).
links.src_t: PMCCF Investment Management Agreement

links.detail: BlackRock (Financial Markets Advisory) served as investment manager for the Secondary Market Corporate Credit Facility (SMCCF), including executing its wind-down sales at the direction of the New York Fed.
links.src_t: New York Fed FAQs: Secondary Market Corporate Credit Facility

links.detail: Investment Management Agreement dated March 25, 2020 between the New York Fed and BlackRock Financial Management, Inc. to support purchases and management of agency commercial mortgage-backed securities for the System Open Market Account.
links.src_t: New York Fed - BlackRock FMA Investment Management Agreement (agency CMBS)

links.detail: State Street Bank and Trust Company is custodian (Custodian Agreement of May 11, 2020) and administrator (Administration Agreement of May 11, 2020) for Corporate Credit Facilities LLC, the New York Fed vehicle for the PMCCF/SMCCF.
links.src_t: PMCCF Investment Management Agreement

links.detail: In May 2020 the New York Fed selected The Bank of New York Mellon as custodian and administrator for TALF 2020.
links.src_t: New York Fed: Term Asset-Backed Securities Loan Facility

links.src_t: Central Banking: ECB hires BlackRock to design ABS programme

pats.title: New York and London banking axis
pats.summary: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is formally owned by its member banks: at end-2018 Citibank held 42.8% of its stock, JPMorgan Chase 29.5% and HSBC's US bank 6.1%, the last with its ultimate parent in London. In the 1920s the partnership of Benjamin Strong (New York Fed) and Montagu Norman (Bank of England, earlier a partner at the merchant bank Brown Shipley) set much of the direction of world finance; in 1925 the New York Fed opened a $200 million gold credit for the Bank of England and J.P. Morgan & Co. a $100 million credit for the British government so that sterling could return to gold. The London houses Morgan Grenfell (half-owned by J.P. Morgan & Co. from 1910) and Brown Shipley (a branch of Brown Brothers until 1914) were London ends of New York banks, and J.P. Morgan & Co. led the American banking group that took the US share of the Bank for International Settlements in 1930. Since 31 October 2013 the Fed and the Bank of England have had a standing swap line.

timeline.event: J.P. Morgan & Co. of New York took 50% of its London house, renamed Morgan, Grenfell & Co. on 1 January 1910.

The New York Fed cut interest rates in 1925 and again in 1927 to help the Bank of England return to, and stay on, gold.

The Fed converted its swap lines with the Bank of England, ECB, Bank of Japan, Bank of Canada and SNB into standing arrangements.

pats.uncertain: Holding Reserve Bank stock is a condition of Fed membership and is not ordinary ownership: it cannot be sold or pledged and voting is limited to electing six of nine directors. Holder-level figures exist only for 2007 and 2018 (via FOIA). No primary source supports Mullins' claim that London merchant banks control the New York banks. The personal Strong-Norman tie is well documented, but how far it set Fed policy is debated by historians and is not settled here.

role_info.New York hub: Home of the New York Fed and of the banks that hold most of its stock.
role_info.London partner: The Bank of England and the London banks tied to the New York houses.
role_info.foreign parent of a holder: A foreign company whose US bank holds New York Fed stock.

pats.implications: The bank that carries out US monetary policy is formally owned by the large commercial banks it supervises and rescues, two of which held nearly three-quarters of its stock in 2018. That stock does not give them control of interest rates, which are set by the Fed's Board and its rate committee, but it does give them seats in the room: they elect six of the New York Fed's nine directors. The 1920s record shows how much of the world's money was steered through a few personal and banking ties between New York and London, outside any vote. For an ordinary reader, the point is that the people closest to the money supply have long been bankers and their partners abroad, not the public. Whether that closeness bends policy today is argued, not proven. The claim that London's merchant banks secretly control the Fed rests on one author and no records.

pats.title: Basel and the central bankers' clubs
pats.summary: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) was set up in Basel in 1930 under the Young Plan to handle German reparations; its first capital came from five European central banks plus a Japanese banking group and an American group led by J.P. Morgan & Co., and its first president was Gates McGarrah, former chairman of the New York Fed. Under a 1987 agreement with Switzerland its premises and archives are inviolable, it is immune from Swiss courts and from seizure of its assets and of deposits placed with it, and it pays no Swiss taxes; it is audited by a private firm (PwC up to the year to March 2026), not by a national audit office. Around it sit the Basel Committee (1974), which writes the bank-capital rules its members commit to apply, the Financial Stability Board (1999/2009), the invitation-only Group of Thirty (1978), which seats serving central bankers beside private bankers, and the Kansas City Fed's Jackson Hole meeting (since 1982).
